title: Avatar System Decisions
summary: Steffen 1 + Steffen 2 coordination document. Avatar system decisions, style direction, character proportions, color palette, BLUE HUD pivot, full Crossy Road character set.
content:
Avatar System Decisions

Steffen 1 + Steffen 2 | 2026-03-16 One creative director, two hands.

DECISION 1: Dual Style System (CONFIRMED)

We maintain TWO character styles, not one. They coexist in the catalog.

Style A: Pixel-Warm (Default, Production)

  • Current sprites in /corner/sprites/
  • 13 agents x 4 states = 52 state sprites
  • 13 agents x 4 directions = 52 walk sprites
  • Total: 104 character assets
  • These are IN PRODUCTION. Bobby's live build uses them.
  • DO NOT change or replace these without a migration plan.

Style B: Crossy Road Chunky (Style Pack, Exploration)

  • FULL SET GENERATED: All 13 agents at 3 sizes (24px, 48px, 128px) = 39 character assets
  • At catalog/characters/crossy-road/{agent}-{size}.png
  • Original 4 characters still at /visual-target/crossy-road-style/character-*.png
  • These are CATALOG items for the marketplace/style pack feature
  • Not yet integrated into the live build

Why Both

The product supports style packs (per Patrik's direction). Default style is pixel-warm. Crossy Road is the first alternate style pack. Users choose. Both need to be complete sets.

DECISION 2: Character Proportions

Pixel-Warm Style

  • Head: ~40% of body height
  • Body: standard proportions, slightly chibi
  • Size at overview zoom: 24-30px
  • Size at detail zoom: 64-80px
  • Size in HUD portraits: 42px (plumbob clip)

Crossy Road Style

  • Head: ~50% of body height (more exaggerated)
  • Body: blocky, 4-5 voxels wide
  • Minimum readable size: 24px (must still read in HUD pills)
  • Maximum detail size: 128px (room close-up)
  • Characters should be recognizable at ANY size between 24-128px
  • The key: PROPS + SIGNATURE COLOR identify the agent, not facial detail

Multi-Size Asset Pipeline (NEW, Steffen 2)

Each Crossy Road character now exists at THREE sizes:

Size Purpose Render Focus
128px Game rooms, detail view, character select Full body + props + ambient glow + personality
48px HUD portrait circles, agent frames Head + shoulders + primary prop + color dominance
24px Pills, status indicators, tiny badges Head silhouette + signature color fill only

At 128px: Full character on platform. All props visible. Ambient glow in signature color. Dynamic pose. At 48px: Head and upper body. Primary prop visible. Signature color dominates. Fits circular HUD frame. At 24px: Pure abstraction. Head shape + color. One prop hint maximum. Color IS the character.

Cross-Style Consistency

  • Both styles use the SAME signature colors per agent
  • Both styles use the SAME props per agent (Bobby = headphones + laptop, Elon = wrench + server, etc.)
  • Both styles occupy the SAME grid footprint (1x1 sub-cell for standing character)
  • The sprite state system (idle, thinking, speaking, done) applies to BOTH styles

DECISION 5: Avatar States

Both styles must support these 5 states. The HUD and game read the state to show the correct sprite/animation.

State Pixel-Warm Expression Crossy Road Expression
idle Sitting at desk, relaxed posture Standing on platform, gentle bob
working Typing, focused lean forward Bouncing in place, arms moving
speaking Mouth open, hand gesture Bouncing higher, speech bubble voxel
thinking Hand on chin, thought bubble Tilted head, rotating question mark voxel
done Leaned back, checkmark Victory hop, star particles

For Crossy Road style specifically:

  • Every state should involve MOVEMENT. Nothing is ever truly still.
  • Idle = gentle bob (2px up/down, 3s cycle)
  • Working = faster bob + arm animation
  • Speaking = hop + speech indicator
  • Thinking = slow tilt rotation
  • Done = big celebratory bounce

DECISION 6: BLUE HUD (NEW, Steffen 2, PATRIK DIRECTIVE)

Date: 2026-03-16 Source: Patrik direct order. "Not warm amber. BLUE." Status: DECIDED. Blue replaces warm amber as the HUD north star.

The Pivot

The warm walnut wood HUD looked cozy but didn't feel like a GAME. Patrik wants BLUE.

Why blue works better:

  • Temperature contrast. Warm office rooms above (amber, orange, wood) + cool blue glass HUD below. Two temperatures on one screen = visual depth + sophistication.
  • Game energy. Blue glass reads as sci-fi cockpit, fighter jet HUD, command center. It says "you are in control." Wood said "you are at home."
  • Status visibility. Red (blocked) on blue = MAXIMUM contrast. Red on warm amber was hard to distinguish. Green on blue also pops cleanly. Blue was the right canvas for status colors all along.
  • Freshness. Blue feels modern, alive, digital. Wood felt retro (which was nice but doesn't match Patrik's energy).

Blue Palette (replaces warm amber)

Role Old (Warm) New (Blue) Notes
Panel base #3E2723 (walnut) #0B1628 (deep navy glass) Frosted glass, not solid
Primary accent #FFB74D (amber) #2196F3 (electric blue) The "hero" color
Secondary accent #FF9800 (orange) #64B5F6 (ice blue) Highlights, hover
Glow color #FFB74D (amber glow) #4FC3F7 (cyan glow) Status glows, active indicators
Text primary #FFF8E1 (cream) #F5F5F5 (white) Higher contrast on blue
Text secondary #E8E0D0 (warm gray) #90CAF9 (blue-gray) Labels, metadata
Glass effect n/a rgba(13, 71, 161, 0.15) + blur Frosted glass is the new material
Panel border #5D4037 (wood edge) rgba(100, 181, 246, 0.2) Subtle blue edge

Material: Blue Frosted Glass

  • NOT solid dark panel. Semi-transparent frosted glass.
  • The warm game world GLOWS THROUGH the blue glass.
  • Where warm office light hits the top of the blue panel, you get a beautiful warm-to-cool transition.
  • Subtle hexagonal noise texture on the glass (like carbon fiber but blue).
  • The glass has depth: lighter center, darker edges.

The Sims Curve: KEPT

The signature curved top edge stays. The curve is the soul of the HUD shape. Now rendered in blue glass instead of walnut wood. The curve catches light differently on glass: more reflective, sharper highlight on the edge, transparency fade at the apex.

DECISION 7: DESIGN REFERENCES (NEW, Steffen 2)

Date: 2026-03-16 Source: Patrik references. These are the NORTH STARS for how the HUD should feel.

Reference 1: Trello Thickness

Everything in the HUD is CHUNKY. Think Trello cards:

  • Fat rounded corners (12-16px border radius)
  • Generous padding (16px minimum inside cards)
  • Thick borders (3px, not thin 1px hairlines)
  • Thick progress bars (12-14px tall, not thin 4px web bars)
  • Components feel like physical objects you could pick up
  • Nothing thin, nothing delicate, nothing "web design"

Implementation rule: If a component looks like it belongs in a Figma prototype, it's too thin. If it looks like a card on a table, it's right.

Reference 2: Vegas Energy (UPDATED Mar 16 Patrik directive)

Text is OVERSIZED. Confident. Impossible to miss:

  • Project names: 20px minimum, bold (Patrik corrected from 16px to 18-20px)
  • Agent names: 18px minimum, semibold
  • Stats numbers: 16px minimum, bold
  • Task counts/badges: 16px minimum
  • Status badges: 14px minimum, uppercase, tracking wide (was 11px, too small)
  • NOTHING below 16px except timestamps (timestamps can be 14px)
  • If you have to squint, it's too small
  • If it doesn't pop at arm's length, scale it up
  • The HUD should be SCANNABLE from a distance

The test: Hold your phone at arm's length. Can you still read the project names? If no, bigger.

Reference 3: "Old People Read Em, Young People Love Em"

This is the universal standard. It's not about age, it's about:

  • HIGH CONTRAST: White text (#F1F5F9) on deep blue (#0F1B2D) = pass
  • READABLE SIZES: Nothing below 16px anywhere in the HUD (except timestamps at 14px)
  • CHUNKY TOUCH TARGETS: Everything clickable is 48px minimum
  • CLEAR HIERARCHY: 3 levels max. Primary (20px/white/bold), secondary (18px/blue-gray), tertiary (16px/dim)
  • SATISFYING INTERACTIONS: Big click targets, visible hover states, generous spacing
  • Agent portraits: 48px with 3px signature color ring (was 32px)

DECISION 8: OPEN QUESTIONS RESOLVED (Steffen 2)

Date: 2026-03-16

Q1: Walk animations for Crossy Road style

DECIDED: HOP. Characters hop between squares, not slide. This is the defining motion of Crossy Road. Each step is a discrete bounce to the next tile. The hop adds personality and ENERGY. Sliding is generic. Hopping is delightful.

Bobby implementation: CSS keyframe animation per hop. 200ms per tile transition. The character lifts 4-6px at the peak. Small shadow compresses/expands below. On landing, a tiny dust puff particle (2-3 small circles that fade out in 300ms).

Q2: HUD avatar size in Crossy Road mode

DECIDED: SWITCH. When the user selects Crossy Road theme, the HUD portraits switch to chunky voxel style too. The HUD and game should feel like ONE product, not two different UIs stapled together. Consistency > flexibility here.

Bobby implementation: The 48px portraits at catalog/characters/crossy-road/{agent}-48.png are designed specifically for the HUD circle frames. Swap the portrait src when the style pack changes. The agent frame rings stay the same (they're style-agnostic).

Q3: Character customization scope

DECIDED: Fixed base + unlockable accessories. The base character design is LOCKED per agent. Bobby = purple headphones + hoodie. That's non-negotiable. But users can unlock/equip accessories that ADD to the base:

  • Hats (santa hat, party hat, crown, hard hat)
  • Particles (sparkles, fire, snow)
  • Pets (tiny companion that follows the agent)
  • Background effects (rainbow trail, confetti, lightning)

Accessories are ADDITIONS, never REPLACEMENTS. The base character must always be recognizable. If an accessory obscures the primary prop, it's a bad accessory.

Generation Script

scripts/generate-crossy-characters.py

  • Usage: python3 scripts/generate-crossy-characters.py [agent|all] [size|all]
  • Can regenerate individual agents or sizes
  • 3s delay between Gemini calls
  • Retry logic: 3 attempts per image with backoff

Design Decisions for Characters

Why these KEY identifiers:

  • Bobby's headphones are visible as a silhouette bump on top of his head even at 24px
  • Cleo's scarf is a color band below the head shape, reads at any size
  • Tony's ring light creates a circular halo BEHIND the head, visible even as a glow
  • Jacob's phone to ear creates an asymmetric silhouette that reads instantly
  • Elmo's lab coat is WHITE, making him the only character with a bright body (stands out in any group)
  • Elon's glowing eyes are two bright green dots that register even at the smallest size
  • Pixel is unique: semi-transparent/glitchy, the only character that breaks the "solid voxel" rule

Differentiation strategy at 24px: At 24px, you can't rely on detail. You rely on:

  1. SIGNATURE COLOR filling most of the space
  2. SILHOUETTE: headphones (Bobby), phone (Jacob), magnifying glass (Elmo), ring light halo (Tony)
  3. BRIGHTNESS: Elmo is bright (white coat), Pixel is dim (transparent), everyone else is standard

FOR STEFFEN 1: Review Checklist

Steffen 2 has generated. Steffen 1 confirms:

  • Blue palette direction: CONFIRMED. Steffen 1 updated hud-blue-spec.md with refined palette (#0F1B2D, #3B82F6, #1E3A5F). Works.
  • Trello thickness: CONFIRMED. 2px borders, 12px radius, 48px portraits with 3px ring. Full spec in hud-blue-spec.md.
  • Vegas text sizing: CORRECTED by Steffen 1. 20px project names, 18px agent names, 16px stats/counts. Patrik said 18-20px minimum.
  • Character consistency: Do all 13 Crossy Road characters feel like the same art style?
  • 24px readability: Can you identify each agent from just the 24px icon?
  • 48px HUD portraits: Do they read clearly inside the agent frame circles?
  • Open questions resolved: HOP, SWITCH, and FIXED+ACCESSORIES all confirmed. Locked.
  • Temperature contrast: CONFIRMED. Warm office (amber/orange) + cool blue HUD = the signature. Full visual target at hud-blue-v1.png.

If any adjustments needed: Update this file with corrections and mark the decision as REVISED. Steffen 2 regenerates.

HANDOFF: Bobby 2

Bobby 2 receives:

  1. Blue HUD visual targets (3 PNGs) as the new north star
  2. Blue component assets (21 PNGs) as direct-use CSS/React sprites
  3. Full Crossy Road character set (39 PNGs) for the character system
  4. Updated HUD integration notes (reference hud-integration-notes.md but apply BLUE palette)

Bobby 2's job: Build the HUD using the blue assets. The warm walnut assets at catalog/hud/ are now DEPRECATED (kept for reference only). The blue assets at catalog/hud-blue/ are the production target.

This document is append-only for decisions. Both Steffens edit. Decisions are final once marked LOCKED.
